title: Freelance Contract Template
description: A general freelance contract to outline scope, payment, and deliverables.
intro: Use this freelance contract to set clear expectations between a freelancer and a client.
whenToUse: When hiring or engaging independent contractors for project work.
template:
This Agreement is between [Client] and [Freelancer].

Scope: [Describe work].
Deliverables: [List].
Payment: [Terms].
Timeline: [Dates].

Signatures:
[Client]
[Freelancer]
example:
This agreement is between Bright Media and Jordan Lee.
Scope: Design landing page.
Payment: $2,000.
Signatures: Bright Media / Jordan Lee

faqs.question: Do I need a contract for small gigs?
faqs.answer: Yes, it helps avoid disputes and clarifies expectations.

title: Freelance Contract Template for Designers

whenToUse: When hiring or contracting with graphic or web designers.
template:
This Agreement is between [Client] and [Designer].

Scope: [Design work].
Deliverables: [Assets].

Payment: [Terms].
example: Logo design project with 3 rounds of revisions and final assets delivered as SVG/PNG.
tips: State ownership transfer on final payment

faqs.question: Who owns the files?
faqs.answer: Ownership can transfer on final payment; specify clearly.

title: Freelance Contract Template for Writers

Payment: [Terms].

faqs.question: Can I republish?
faqs.answer: Depends on the license agreed; specify usage rights.

Payment: [Terms].
example: Design and build 5 pages, handoff CMS access, payment in 2 installments.

faqs.question: Who provides hosting?
faqs.answer: Specify whether developer or client handles hosting and costs.

Scope: [Services].
Deliverables: [Reports].
Confidentiality: [Clause].

faqs.question: Should I include an NDA?
faqs.answer: Yes, attach or reference an NDA if sensitive information is shared.

title: Non-Compete Addendum
description: A short addendum restricting competition for a defined period and geography.

example: No solicitation of clients within 50 miles for 12 months post-termination.

faqs.answer: Enforceability varies by jurisdiction — seek legal advice.

title: Professional Wedding Planner Contract Template
description: A comprehensive contract for wedding planners covering services, payment, cancellation, and liability.
intro: This contract formalizes the relationship between the Wedding Planner ("Planner") and the Client for planning, coordination, and execution of wedding services.
whenToUse: Use this template when entering into an engagement to plan or coordinate a wedding or related events.
template:
Parties:
Planner: [Planner Name], [Address], [Contact].
Client: [Client Name], [Address], [Contact].

1. Services:
Planner agrees to provide planning and coordination services as detailed in Schedule A (the "Services"). Services may include vendor management, timeline creation, venue coordination, and event-day management.

2. Term:
This Agreement commences on [Start Date] and continues until completion of the Services or earlier termination as described herein.

3. Fees and Payment:
Total Fee: $[Total Amount].
Deposit: $[Deposit Amount] due to secure date (non-refundable except as set out herein).
Payment Schedule: [Milestone / date schedule].
Late Fees: Overdue amounts may incur interest at [rate].

4. Expenses:
Client will reimburse Planner for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses (vendor deposits, travel, rentals) incurred while providing Services, provided Planner obtains Client approval for expenses above $[threshold].

5. Cancellation and Refunds:
If Client cancels more than [X] days before event: refund of paid amounts minus non-refundable deposit and confirmed vendor commitments.
If cancellation within [X] days: no refund of deposit and Client remains responsible for unpaid vendor commitments secured by Planner.

6. Vendor Contracts and Payments:
Planner may negotiate vendor agreements on Client’s behalf but is not a party to most vendor contracts unless explicitly stated. Client is ultimately responsible for payments due to vendors unless Planner agrees otherwise in writing.

7. Liability and Insurance:
Planner will exercise reasonable care in performing Services but is not liable for vendor performance, acts of God, or other events outside Planner’s control. Client is encouraged to maintain event insurance.

8. Force Majeure:
Neither party will be liable for delays or failures caused by events beyond reasonable control (e.g., natural disasters, strikes, governmental actions).

9. Cancellation by Planner:
Planner may cancel for material breach by Client or factors that make performance impossible; deposits may be refunded minus costs incurred.

10. Confidentiality and Publicity:
Planner and Client agree to keep sensitive information confidential. Planner may use non-identifying images of the event for promotional purposes unless Client opts out in writing.

11. Termination:
Either party may terminate for material breach if the breach remains uncured after [days] notice. Termination does not relieve Client of obligations to pay for Services provided or costs incurred prior to termination.

12. Dispute Resolution:
Parties agree to attempt mediation before pursuing litigation, and venue for disputes will be [Jurisdiction].

13. Miscellaneous:
Entire Agreement: This document and Schedule A constitute the full agreement.
Amendments: Any changes must be in writing and signed by both parties.
Governing Law: [State/Country law applies].

Signatures:
Planner: ____________________ Date: ________
Client: ____________________ Date: ________
example: This Agreement is between Everlasting Events and Jordan Lee for a wedding on June 20. Services include full planning, vendor coordination, and day-of management. Deposit $2,000. Balance paid in three installments.
tips: Keep the deposit non-refundable only to cover commitments

faqs.question: What if a vendor doesn't perform?
faqs.answer: The Planner will assist in resolving issues, but vendor performance is generally the vendor's responsibility; contract limits Planner liability.

faqs.question: Can I change the guest count later?
faqs.answer: Major changes may affect pricing and vendor commitments; notify Planner as soon as possible.
